name: Question 5
worked_solution:
First, we note that 

$$
F(t)=\int {F}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t=\int ⟨6{t}^{3}+8,\,{e}^{t+1}⟩\text{d}t.
$$

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨6{t}^{3}+8,\,{e}^{t+1}⟩\text{d}t & =⟨\int (6{t}^{3}+8)\,\text{d}t,\int {e}^{t+1}\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3{t}^{4}}{2}+8t+{c}_{1},\,{e}^{t+1}+{c}_{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3{t}^{4}}{2}+8t,\,{e}^{t+1}⟩+⟨{c}_{1},\,{c}_{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3{t}^{4}}{2}+8t,\,{e}^{t+1}⟩+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary (vector) constant of integration.

Question 5
?

If F′(t)=⟨6t3+8,et+1⟩, then F(t)=

a
⟨3t4+8t,et+1⟩+C
b
⟨t42+8t,et+1⟩+C
c
⟨3t42+8t,et−1⟩+C
d
⟨3t42+8t,et+1⟩+C
e
⟨4t23,et⟩+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that F(t)=∫F′(t)dt=∫⟨6t3+8,et+1⟩dt.

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we get

∫⟨6t3+8,et+1⟩dt=⟨∫(6t3+8)dt,∫et+1dt⟩=⟨3t42+8t+c1,et+1+c2⟩=⟨3t42+8t,et+1⟩+⟨c1,c2⟩=⟨3t42+8t,et+1⟩+C,

where C is an arbitrary (vector) constant of integration.
